why.emptyGroup: is an empty group, which matches nothing

bind.noValueIgnored: {{word}}: names no value and was ignored
bind.valueNotScope: {{word}}: takes a value, not a scope
bind.negatedRowCount: the minus cannot negate a row count — negating a pair is not negating its halves

axis.takesQuoted: {{word}} takes {{hint}} — a quoted value is text
axis.noRegex: the {{word}} axis cannot run one — regular expressions run on text and file paths only

pattern.pathWeak: a pattern on a file path rarely helps — path names run words together
pattern.unclosed: the pattern was not closed — it ends at whitespace, so a space is written \s

value.glued: two values are glued together — a space is missing
value.exactPattern: exact and a pattern cannot combine
value.trailingRange: {{written}} reads as at least {{bound}} — the same as {{wildcard}} for the upper bound
value.punctuationOnly: punctuation is not matched — search it as a pattern

scope.innerBindScope: an axis inside a scope takes a value, not a scope
scope.twoKinds: a row is one kind — {{a}} and {{b}} never share one, so this can match nothing
scope.nested: a scope cannot hold another scope
scope.emptyMeansAny: {{word}}:{} means any {{word}} row — the same as {{word}}:*
scope.unclosedBeforeNext: the scope was not closed — closed it before the next clause
scope.unclosedAtEnd: the scope was not closed — closed it at the end
scope.needsPositive: a scope needs a positive term — negation only refines
scope.contentNegation: both sides are content words, which rarely share one row — negate a kind word or a property instead
scope.qualifierAlone: a {{name}} only says who a row plays on — add what the row is
scope.foreignAxis: a {{word}} axis cannot read a {{column}} row

simplify.allDead: every alternative of this query contradicts itself; it is returned as written
simplify.matchesEverything: this query matches every spell — one alternative selects whatever the other excludes — so its simplest form is the empty query

sort.takesDoor: {{word}} takes a door word to order by, as in {{word}}{{bind}}name or {{word}}{{bind}}{{negate}}model
sort.takesCount: {{word}} takes how many to list, as in {{word}}{{bind}}20
